unit.name: Project framing: speed first, then architecture choices
unit.description: The lecture frames AI project strategy with a wake-word lamp example and argues that fast iteration, broad literature search, open-source baselines, and expert conversations usually matter more than prematurely optimizing architecture details.
unit.summary: The lecture opens by arguing that AI teams can differ by 10x or more in productivity because stronger teams make better next-step decisions, not just better algorithmic choices [ts=64s] [ts=103s]. Using an offline voice-controlled lamp that responds to "Robert, turn on" as the running example, the instructor advises building something quickly instead of over-deliberating among plausible designs [ts=691s] [ts=704s]. He notes that general-purpose speech recognition is often too heavy for a cheap on-device product, whereas a specialized wake-word detector can be much smaller [ts=722s] [ts=755s]. The recommended first moves are a broad literature/open-source search and respectful outreach to experts, because both compress the time needed to converge on workable approaches [ts=842s] [ts=960s].

key_points.text: Project execution speed can create order-of-magnitude productivity differences in AI teams.
A lightweight wake-word model is often more practical on-device than full speech-to-text.
Skim broadly across papers and repos before deeply reading a few high-value resources.
Contacting experts after doing your own homework can sharply accelerate learning.

kp_catalog.name: Iteration speed as a core AI project lever
kp_catalog.description: The idea that faster experiment-selection and execution loops matter more than small local modeling choices because they compound over time.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: Iteration speed frames the project-strategy mindset but is not a technical prerequisite gate.

kp_catalog.name: Broad literature search before deep implementation
kp_catalog.description: A strategy of skimming many papers, posts, and repos first, then going deep only on the most informative resources.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The wake-word case explicitly recommends literature/open-source search as the fastest early accelerator before custom implementation [ts=842s] [ts=903s].

kp_catalog.name: Expert outreach as a learning multiplier
kp_catalog.description: A pragmatic tactic of asking knowledgeable authors or domain experts for help after doing initial homework.
kp_catalog.importance_rationale: The instructor presents short conversations with experts as high-ROI accelerators once you have already tried to understand the problem yourself [ts=960s] [ts=1040s].
